title: Goodwill NCW highlights ways for communities to give back on Giving Tuesday
text:
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
Ashley DeMuth, CEO | Menomonie Area Chamber of Commerce
Goodwill North Central Wisconsin (NCW) will participate in Giving Tuesday on December 3, encouraging community members to support its mission through several avenues. The organization aims to make it simple for people to have a local impact by donating items, rounding up purchases, making financial contributions, or shopping at its stores.
The nonprofit reports that individuals served by its programs collectively increased their annual income by more than $4.5 million last year across north central Wisconsin. Goodwill NCW provides job training and employment services funded primarily through retail sales generated from donated goods. Each donation is said to support about three hours of job skill training.
From December 2 through December 15, shoppers can choose to round up their purchase totals at the register by $1 or more as part of the Goodwill NCW Giving Tree initiative. Those who participate will receive an ornament to place on Giving Trees located in the organization’s 27 retail locations.
Financial donations can also be made online at Financial Donation | Goodwill NCW. According to the organization, approximately 90 cents of every dollar spent in its stores goes back into supporting its mission: “Elevating People by Eliminating Barriers to Employment.”
In a statement, Goodwill NCW expressed appreciation for community support: "During this season of giving, Goodwill NCW would like to thank shoppers and donors for their ongoing support to transform lives."
The organization describes itself as dedicated to understanding and addressing community needs while empowering individuals and families through skill-building for sustainable employment and improved financial stability.
